title: A Hair-Thin Stream of Water Can Cut Through Steel

scenes.text: A stream of water as thin as a hair can cut steel.
Machines pump water to about sixty thousand pounds per square inch.
It shoots out of a tiny diamond or sapphire nozzle.
The jet moves faster than the speed of sound.
Mix in crushed garnet, and it slices steel, granite and armor plate.
And it uses only about half a gallon of water a minute.
No flame. No blade. Just a hair-thin stream of water.

description:
A stream of water as thin as a hair can cut steel.
At around 60,000 psi, the jet leaves a tiny diamond or sapphire nozzle faster than the speed of sound. Add crushed garnet and it cuts steel, granite and armor plate.
What would you cut first?
first_comment: Bonus: the abrasive garnet is drawn into the stream by suction and makes the jet vastly more powerful. Could you cut glass with it?
